nodes.title: Hiding a window on close strands foreground + accessibility focus on the invisible window (Windows MSAA/UIA) - screen readers keep reading the closed app
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.5.0; Reproduced in shipping apps on current Electron/Chromium builds (OpenAI Codex, Anthropic Claude desktop).  Codex: Version 26.616.81150 Claude 1.15200.0 (250bae) 2026-06-23T05:40:53.000Z

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 (build 26100.8655)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

When a top-level `BrowserWindow` is hidden in response to a close (e.g. the app intercepts `close` and calls `win.hide()` to keep running in the background), the window should relinquish foreground activation and clear its focused accessibility state. Windows then activates the next window in the Z-order, and that window's process emits `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND`, so assistive technology (Narrator, JAWS, NVDA) follows focus to the new foreground.

### Actual Behavior

On Alt+F4, the window's pixels disappear but it is **hidden, not destroyed**, and it **never relinquishes foreground activation or its focused accessibility state**:

- The top-level window fires `EVENT_OBJECT_HIDE` while still reporting `STATE_SYSTEM_FOCUSED` (state `0x168004`).
- The render-widget child is reparented offscreen (`0x118000`) and moved to the origin.
- No `EVENT_OBJECT_DESTROY` is fired.
- No `EVENT_SYSTEM_FOREGROUND` to any successor window is fired.
- `GetForegroundWindow()` immediately after the close still returns the now-invisible window's HWND (also visible inline in the events' `ForegroundWnd` field).

Because foreground is never released, Windows never activates a successor, so no process emits a foreground/focus event. Screen readers have nothing to follow and keep reading the closed app. With Narrator, "Say current line" (Insert+Up) still reads the closed window's chat content after the window is gone.


### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/v-tab-vispero/640ea5acbf40c6c14ce547b8254d0ee2

### Additional Information

### Accessibility impact
Screen-reader users cannot perceive that the window closed, focus is stranded on a dead window, and they continue to hear the closed app with no path back to the real foreground. This affects any Electron app that hides-on-close (Signal/Element/Discord are cited in #48268 on Linux; Codex/Claude/Whisper Flow on Windows).

### Suggested fix
When a `BrowserWindow` is hidden while it is the active/foreground window, the hide path should release foreground activation, clear `STATE_SYSTEM_FOCUSED`, and emit the platform deactivation/focus-out accessibility event so the OS and AT can hand off. 

### Related
- #48268 - Hidden windows present themselves as active to Linux screenreaders (at-spi). Same defect, Linux side.
- #10023 - `win.hide()` does not focus the background window on Windows. `win.blur()` workaround.
- #405 - Restore focus to the previous application, when Cerebro closes

nodes.title: Drop support for Linux distributions that are EOL
nodes.body:
Our docs for Linux support:

https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/f02df6edb4ada66fa3c76c851ffff5fd9a2916cd/README.md?plain=1#L42-L45

For example, [Debian 10](https://www.debian.org/releases/buster/) is EOL. Ubuntu 18 is, too.

Dropping support needs to be done in a major version.

We might want to change our support policy and wording here to say that we support all versions of Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian that are still supported by the disto makers. ### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

42.4.1, 37.6.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 25H2, Build 26200.8655 (UBR 8655). Cumulative updates KB5094135 (2026-06-09) and KB5094126 (2026-06-10) installed.

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown — crashes began 2026-06-16, immediately after the June 2026 cumulative update; the Electron app versions were unchanged across that boundary.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

The GPU (and renderer) child process launches normally under the sandbox.

### Actual Behavior

The GPU process is killed by EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT (0x80000003 / exit_code=-2147483645) immediately on launch, **before any GPU vendor DLL is loaded**. The browser process retries 6 times within ~0.3s and then self-terminates.

Browser process log (captured with --enable-logging=stderr --v=1):

​```
[ERROR:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:996] GPU process exited unexpectedly: exit_code=-2147483645
[WARNING:content\browser\gpu\gpu_process_host.cc:1438] The GPU process has crashed 1 time(s)
... (repeats up to 6 times) ...
[FATAL:content\browser\gpu\gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc:417] GPU process isn't usable. Goodbye.
​```

WER signature: faulting module = the app exe itself (statically-linked Chromium), exception code 80000003, identical fault offset across 70+ crash reports.

**A/B isolation (this is the key evidence):**
- Default (GPU sandbox ON): GPU process dies with 0x80000003, 6 times → browser gives up.
- `--disable-gpu-sandbox`: GPU process **survives** (falls back to swiftshader-webgl). No 0x80000003.
- For Notion, `--disable-gpu-sandbox` keeps the main process alive but the **renderer** still crashes (white screen); only `--no-sandbox` makes the renderer survive.

So: sandbox ON → child process dies during sandbox init; sandbox OFF → it lives. This points to a sandbox-init incompatibility, not a GPU driver fault (no vendor DLL is even loaded at crash time) and not third-party DLL injection (the sandboxed children can't be injected).

Google Chrome 149 on the same machine is unaffected — likely because its newer Chromium already handles the changed Windows behavior.

Hardware: NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU (driver 32.0.15.9174) + AMD Radeon 610M (32.0.13034.7001), hybrid graphics laptop.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

A user on the Obsidian forum reports an identical signature (0x80000003, GPU process dies before vendor DLLs load, "GPU process isn't usable") on a different machine (AMD Radeon 780M, Windows 11 24H2), suggesting this is a broader Chromium/Electron sandbox incompatibility with recent Windows builds rather than a single-machine issue: https://forum.obsidian.md/t/gpu-process-crash-report/105321

### Problem Description

The [Electron docs](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/extensions) explicitly state it's a non-goal to support all extension capabilities. This makes sense, since many APIs (e.g. `chrome.tabs.create()`) don't have a clear representation at the Electron platform level.

But applications should be able to customize these API behaviors to suit their needs and provide richer support for more extensions.

### Proposed Solution

Something like a preload script whereby applications can extend or modify the `chrome.*` APIs to suit their needs. This allows high flexibility for applications to control the behavior while keeping the bulk of the maintenance cost (supporting new APIs etc) off of Electron.

### Alternatives Considered

Expose first-class APIs to register handlers for chrome extension APIs. This gives a clear surface for applications and may allow cleaner implementation (e.g. return a WebContents -> Electron converts it to the `Tab` interface for you) but puts a heavy maintenance burden on Electron.

### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.10.3

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test.

This uses Electron's `BrowserWindow` API (`enableLargerThanScreen`, `showInactive`, `setBounds`, `getBounds`) and I do not know of a direct equivalent surface in Google Chrome to create a transparent frameless native window spanning arbitrary display bounds.

### Expected Behavior

A frameless transparent `BrowserWindow` created with valid virtual-screen bounds should remain at the requested bounds after being shown.

In the repro environment, `screen.getAllDisplays()` reports this layout:

```text
Primary built-in Retina display: bounds { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1512, height: 982 }, scaleFactor: 2
External display A:             bounds { x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 2560, height: 1440 }, scaleFactor: 1
External display B:             bounds { x: 800, y: -1440, width: 2560, height: 1440 }, scaleFactor: 1
```

The virtual display union is:

```text
{ x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
```

After creating and showing a single `BrowserWindow` at that union rectangle, `win.getBounds()` should continue to report:

```text
{ x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
```

The same should hold after explicitly reapplying the same bounds with `setBounds()` while the window is already visible.

### Actual Behavior

The window initially reports the requested bounds correctly. Shortly after `showInactive()` emits `show`, Electron emits a native `move`/`moved` event and `getBounds()` jumps to a different position while preserving width/height:

```text
requested: { x: -1760, y: -1440, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
actual:    { x: -3520, y: -2422, width: 5120, height: 2422 }
```

Example output from the standalone repro:

```text
PROBE before-showInactive {"t":152,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE after-showInactive {"t":152,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE event-show {"t":163,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE event-move {"t":208,"bounds":{"x":-3520,"y":-2422,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-3520,-2422]}
PROBE event-moved {"t":208,"bounds":{"x":-3520,"y":-2422,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-3520,-2422]}
```

This is not caused by app code reapplying incorrect bounds. In `PROBE_MODE=passive`, the script does not call `setBounds()` after `showInactive()`, but the native `move` event still occurs.

If the correct bounds are explicitly reapplied after the window is already visible, the synchronous read-back is correct, then the same delayed native move happens again:

```text
PROBE after-reapply-1500ms {"t":1675,"bounds":{"x":-1760,"y":-1440,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-1760,-1440]}
PROBE event-move {"t":1783,"bounds":{"x":-3520,"y":-2422,"width":5120,"height":2422},"position":[-3520,-2422]}
```

No `display-metrics-changed` event fires during the move.

The trigger appears to be a single frameless window spanning the seam between display rows with different `scaleFactor` values: the external displays are above the primary display (`y < 0`, scale factor 1), while the primary Retina display starts at `y = 0` (scale factor 2). Windows contained inside a single display's bounds are stable.

I also inspected the move with LLDB. Immediately before the Electron `move` event, the native stack includes AppKit's `NSWindow` constraint/move path:

```text
AppKit`-[NSWindow constrainFrameRect:toScreen:]
Electron Framework ...
Electron Framework ...
AppKit`-[NSWindow _overrideDefeatingConstrainFrameRect:toScreen:fullScreenConstrainToTile:]
AppKit`-[NSWindow _setFrameAfterMove:]
AppKit`-[NSWindow _windowMovedToRect:dueToMoveEvent:]
AppKit`-[NSWindow _windowMoved:]
```

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/5Hyeons/48a58a446f1e6bf0fe80d45c3803c8da

### Additional Information

The affected window options are:

```js
new BrowserWindow({
  x: -1760,
  y: -1440,
  width: 5120,
  height: 2422,
  transparent: true,
  frame: false,
  hasShadow: false,
  resizable: false,
  movable: false,
  focusable: false,
  show: false,
  backgroundColor: '#00000000',
  enableLargerThanScreen: true,
  hiddenInMissionControl: true,
  roundedCorners: false,
  webPreferences: { backgroundThrottling: false }
})
```

Observed stable cases in the same display layout:

42.3.0

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Arch (Wayland)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

A directory-less `defaultPath` should set the suggested filename only and must not
produce a relative `current_folder` — matching the macOS and Windows behavior.

### Actual Behavior

The `SaveFile` options carry a valid `current_name` but a relative `current_folder`:

```
   array [
      dict entry(
         string "current_name"
         variant             string "test.jpeg"
      )
      dict entry(
         string "current_folder"
         variant             array of bytes "." + \0
      )
   ]
```

Real-world capture from the Flatpak Signal (`org.signal.Signal`, Electron 42.3.0):

```
... member=SaveFile
   string "org.signal.Signal"
   string "wayland:..."
   string "All Files"
   array [
      dict entry(
         string "current_name"
         variant             string "signal-2026-05-24-214530.jpeg"
      )
      dict entry(
         string "current_folder"
         variant             array of bytes "." + \0
      )
   ]
```

The dialog's location becomes `file:.` (an unusable relative path). With the LXQt
backend the filename field also comes up empty.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This is a problem I hit with the Flatpak version of Signal when saving files through
the Linux file-chooser portal — it looks like it can be fixed in Electron's Linux
dialog code (details below). Reproduced with the LXQt portal backend, but the
malformed request is sent regardless of backend.

This report was drafted with AI assistance; the `dbus-monitor` capture is from my
own machine and the code references point to the linked diffs, so it can all be
verified directly.

## Summary

On Linux, `dialog.showSaveDialog` / `dialog.showOpenDialog` with a **directory-less
`defaultPath`** (a bare filename — which the docs explicitly permit) sends
`current_folder="."` in the xdg-desktop-portal `SaveFile` request. The relative `.`
is not a usable directory: the dialog opens at a broken location (shown as
`file:.`), and on stricter portal backends the suggested filename is dropped too.
macOS and Windows handle the identical input correctly.

## Platform

- Linux, Wayland
- xdg-desktop-portal FileChooser interface v4
- Reproduced with the LXQt portal backend (empty filename **and** `file:.`). The
  malformed `current_folder="."` is produced by Electron/Chromium and sent to
  whichever backend is configured; how visible the breakage is depends on the
  backend (GTK tolerates the `.` and still prefills the name; LXQt does not).

## Steps to reproduce

Minimal main-process snippet:

```js
const { app, dialog } = require('electron')
app.whenReady().then(async () => {
  // bare filename, no directory — allowed per the docs
  await dialog.showSaveDialog({ defaultPath: 'test.jpeg' })
})
```

While the dialog is open, watch the portal call:

```
dbus-monitor --session "interface='org.freedesktop.impl.portal.FileChooser',member='SaveFile'"
```

## Root cause

`shell/browser/ui/file_dialog_linux.cc` forwards `settings.default_path` to
`SelectFile` unmodified whenever it is non-empty:

```cpp
base::FilePath default_path = settings.default_path.empty()
                                  ? electron::GetDefaultPath()
                                  : settings.default_path;
dialog_->SelectFile(..., default_path, ...);
```

A bare filename is non-empty, so it is passed straight through, and Chromium's
portal layer then derives `current_folder` from `DirName()` → `"."`.

macOS and Windows guard against exactly this:

- `file_dialog_mac.mm` — sets the directory only `if (default_path.IsAbsolute())`,
  otherwise uses `BaseName()` as the filename and leaves the directory unset.
- `file_dialog_win.cc` — `SetFileName(BaseName)` and only calls `SetDefaultFolder`
  `if (default_path.IsAbsolute())`.

The Linux path has no equivalent `IsAbsolute()` guard. The recent "default to
Downloads folder" PRs (#49441 → #49538 → #49868, targeting 43.0) only handle the
**empty** `defaultPath` case and leave this code path untouched.

### Electron Version

41.0.0 through 42.4.1 (latest stable at time of filing). Also reproduces on v43.0.0-alpha.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

All

### Operating System Version

N/A

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

40.8.5 (and the rest of the 40.x line) for the duplexMode / printBackground options. See the separate note below on default-duplex inheritance, which is longstanding.

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

For `webContents.print()` (silent path):

- Passing `duplexMode: 'longEdge' | 'shortEdge' | 'simplex'` should take effect.
- Passing `printBackground: true` should print background graphics.
- This is how 40.x behaves.
- Also, omitting `duplexMode` should letting the printer/driver default duplex apply during silent printing


### Actual Behavior

Since 41.0.0, in `webContents.print()`:

1. An explicitly supplied `duplexMode` is **ignored** — the job always prints simplex.
2. An explicitly supplied `printBackground` is **ignored** — backgrounds are never printed.

(Both options still work in `printToPDF()`, which is a different, separately-normalized code path.)

3. `duplexMode` defaulting to simplex when no value is supplied. There is no way to request "use the printer's configured default."

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Hedwig188/c10ef911b9a55921eb49c404d9118816

### Additional Information

## Root Cause

In `shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_contents.cc`, `WebContents::Print` reads several caller options out of the JS `options` dictionary using Chromium's internal **print-settings key constants** instead of the public JS option names.

The JS layer does not rename options: `WebContents.prototype.print` in `lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts` passes the caller's `options` object straight to the native `_print` binding (only `pageSize` is transformed into `mediaSize`). So native receives the public names, e.g. `duplexMode` and `printBackground`.

Most option reads survive only because the Chromium key string coincidentally equals the JS option name:

| JS option | native reads under | string value | matches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | `printing::kSettingColor` | `"color"` | yes |
| `landscape` | `printing::kSettingLandscape` | `"landscape"` | yes |
| `deviceName` | `printing::kSettingDeviceName` | `"deviceName"` | yes |
| `scaleFactor` | `printing::kSettingScaleFactor` | `"scaleFactor"` | yes |
| `pagesPerSheet` | `printing::kSettingPagesPerSheet` | `"pagesPerSheet"` | yes |
| `collate` | `printing::kSettingCollate` | `"collate"` | yes |
| `copies` | `printing::kSettingCopies` | `"copies"` | yes |
| **`duplexMode`** | `printing::kSettingDuplexMode` | **`"duplex"`** | **no** |
| **`printBackground`** | `printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds` | **`"shouldPrintBackgrounds"`** | **no** |

The string values are from Chromium `printing/print_job_constants.cc`.

Because the JS object never contains a `"duplex"` or `"shouldPrintBackgrounds"` key, those two reads never match and always return their fallbacks (`kSimplex` / `false`), which are then written into the settings.

### duplexMode

**40.8.5 (working):**

```cpp
// Duplex type user wants to use.
const auto duplex_mode = options.ValueOrDefault(
    "duplexMode", printing::mojom::DuplexMode::kSimplex);
settings.Set(printing::kSettingDuplexMode, static_cast<int>(duplex_mode));
```

**41.0.0+ (broken):**

```cpp
// Duplex type user wants to use.
const auto duplex_mode = options.ValueOrDefault(
    printing::kSettingDuplexMode, printing::mojom::DuplexMode::kSimplex);
settings.Set(printing::kSettingDuplexMode, static_cast<int>(duplex_mode));
```

`printing::kSettingDuplexMode` is `"duplex"`, not `"duplexMode"`.

### printBackground

**40.8.5 (working):**

```cpp
settings.Set(printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds,
             options.ValueOrDefault("printBackground", false));
```

**41.0.0+ (broken):**

```cpp
settings.Set(
    printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds,
    options.ValueOrDefault(printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds, false));
```

`printing::kSettingShouldPrintBackgrounds` is `"shouldPrintBackgrounds"`, not `"printBackground"`. (Note: v41 even defines a correct local constant `kPrintBackground = "printBackground"`, but the read does not use it.)

Both regressions were introduced by the 41.0.0 printing refactor that added `usePrinterDefaultPageSize` (#49812), which switched these reads to `kSetting*` constants. The other options were unaffected only by the coincidence above.

## Separate (longstanding) issue: cannot inherit the printer's default duplex

Independent of the regression: `WebContents::Print` *always* writes `kSettingDuplexMode`, defaulting to simplex when no value is supplied. This is true in 40.x as well. As a result, omitting `duplexMode` forces simplex rather than letting the printer/driver default duplex apply during silent printing — there is no way to request "use the printer's configured default."

Suggested handling: only set `kSettingDuplexMode` when the caller actually supplied a value, so an omitted `duplexMode` leaves the driver default intact.

### Electron Version

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Insider Preview, build 26200.8117 (24H2, Dev Channel)

### What arch are you using?

Not known — likely an Insider Build + Electron 42 specific issue.
